To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

metastable cubic and, for the first time, tetragonal zrO2 nanoparticles can be obtained by thermal oxidation of zirconium dichalcogenides at temperatures considerably lower than the thermodynamic stability range of these polymorphs.
metastable zirconium dioxide phases can be prepared by the topotactic reactions of ZrS2 and ZrSe2 with oxygen or air.
zirconium dichalcogenides are converted to metastable cubic and/or tetragonal zirconi- um dioxide by thermal oxidation in air.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization and applications of nanostructured materials.
the preparation of nanocrystallites of the metastable cubic and the tetragonal modification of zirconium dioxide by thermal oxidation of zirconium dichalcogenides, ZrS2 and ZrSe2.
the preparation of metastable phases of zirconia by the thermal oxidation of the respective dichalcogenides in air or oxygen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
zirconium disulphide and zirconia are not isotypic and that the reaction of zirconium dichalcogenide with oxygen is not topotactic.

the thermal oxidation of zirconium dichalcogenides is an efficient method for the preparation of metastable zirconia, which can also be used as precursor for the preparation of other zirconium oxides.

the reactions of zirconyl dichalcogenides with oxygen or air proceed topotacti­ cally, yielding metastable cubic and/or tetragonal zir­ conium dioxide at temperatures below the stability range of the metastable polymorphs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reactions of zirconia with sulfur or selenium, respectively, are a new way to prepare metastable zirconia phases.
we have succeeded to prepare metastable cubic and/or tetragonal z- and t-zirconia, respectively, by a topotactic reaction at low temperatures.
the oxidation of zirconium dichalcogenides is a promising method for the preparation of metastable zirconium dioxide phases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metastable ZrO _{2} phases can be obtained by a simple thermal treatment.
the reaction between the dichalcogenide and oxygen is not limited to a simple replacement of sulfur and selenium with oxygen.
metastable zirconium oxides may be obtained in a single step by thermal oxidation of zirconium chalcogenides.
